source: Cambodian MAFF/agricultural extension PowerPoint-derived presentation titled "ដំណាំឪឡឹក" (Watermelon), 42 slides; no presenter, publisher, or date named on the slides reviewed. This presentation exists as two near-identical PDF copies in the source set (one with a green-themed slide design, one plain black-on-white reformat of the same 42 slides) - treat as one source, not two corroborating sources.
text:
Watermelon (ដំណាំឪឡឹក) originated in the dry, savanna regions of Africa. There are four recognized species in the genus: Citrullus Lanatus, Citrullus Colocynthis, Citrullus Ecirrhosus, and Citrullus Naudinianus.

Taxonomically, watermelon belongs to the family Cucurbitaceae, genus Citrullus. Its scientific (species) name is Citrullus Lanatus, and its English common name is Watermelon.

The plant's roots, stems, leaves, and flowers were described: watermelon has separate male and female flowers on the same plant (monoecious), and flowering/pollination activity occurs in the morning, generally between 7 and 11 o'clock.
